source_metadata.title: Acenocoumarol and Heparin Compared with Acenocoumarol Alone in the Initial Treatment of Proximal-Vein Thrombosis
source_metadata.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
source_metadata.metadata_verification: DOI, title, authors, date, and citation verified against the NEJM DOI metadata page; atom content itself was extracted from the retrieved PDF.
source_metadata.text_layer_note: Embedded text layer contained only the download footer; extraction used rendered page images as the authoritative source.

limitations: The PDF text layer was unusable beyond the download footer; extraction was performed from rendered page images.
The article reports several event rates and P values but does not report confidence intervals for the principal comparisons.
Three atoms contain explicitly calculated effect summaries from source-reported counts and are labeled calculated_from_reported_data; these are not author-reported statistics.
No conflict-of-interest statement or data-availability statement was identified in the five-page source.

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial compared the efficacy and safety of continuous intravenous heparin plus acenocoumarol with acenocoumarol alone for the initial treatment of proximal-vein thrombosis.
The study was randomized and double-blind, enrolled symptomatic outpatients with proximal-vein thrombosis, and followed patients for six months.
At early termination, 120 consecutive patients with proximal-vein thrombosis had been enrolled, with 60 assigned to each treatment group.

atoms.canonical_statement: The heparin infusion rate was adjusted daily to maintain the activated partial-thromboplastin time between 60 and 90 seconds, corresponding to about two to three times the mean normal control value.
Acenocoumarol was given as 6 mg on day 1 and 4 mg on day 2, then adjusted using daily prothrombin-time results to an INR target of 2.0 to 3.0; therapy continued for 12 weeks.
Intravenous study medication was continued for at least seven days and then stopped when two consecutive prothrombin-time measurements were in the therapeutic range.
Within 24 hours of randomization, baseline perfusion-ventilation lung scanning and chest radiography were obtained; perfusion-ventilation scanning and venography were repeated after one week.

Patients were examined daily during hospitalization, were instructed to return immediately for symptoms of recurrent venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism after discharge, and were routinely reassessed at 6, 12, and 24 weeks.
Diagnostic tests for suspected recurrent thromboembolism were interpreted independently by an experienced panel blinded to treatment assignment and to whether a test was baseline or repeated.
The primary outcome was confirmed symptomatic extension or recurrence of venous thromboembolism during six months of follow-up.

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial was originally designed for at least 250 patients to detect a twofold increase in symptomatic extension or recurrent venous thromboembolism with 80% power at a two-sided alpha of 0.05, using Fisher’s exact test for group comparisons.

Recruitment was stopped early by the independent Data Safety and Monitoring Committee after an interim analysis showed a high rate of symptomatic extension or recurrence in the acenocoumarol-alone group.

The two randomized groups had similar reported baseline characteristics; mean age was 58±16 versus 56±18 years, women numbered 35 versus 30, and median symptom duration was 10 versus 11 days in the combined-therapy and acenocoumarol-alone groups, respectively.

atoms.canonical_statement: Study medication was interrupted in seven patients: five in the combined-therapy group and two in the acenocoumarol-alone group; none of these patients had recurrent venous thromboembolism or died during six-month follow-up.
Both groups reached the lower therapeutic INR limit of 2.0 after approximately three to four days.
The two treatment groups did not differ significantly in acenocoumarol dose or INR during the first week.
Mean unfractionated-heparin doses, excluding the 5000-unit loading dose, were 29,890, 29,045, 26,835, and 24,728 units on study days 1 through 4, respectively.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that patients with proximal-vein thrombosis require initial treatment with full-dose heparin.
The authors concluded that full-dose heparin can be safely combined with acenocoumarol therapy begun at the same time as heparin.
